## Check your understanding

This check focuses on the network computation, not on decoding, which is covered in the [generation lesson](../generation.qmd).

1. Which operation lets a position incorporate information from other positions, and which one transforms each position independently?
2. Why does a residual connection not replace the transformation computed by a sublayer?

<details>
<summary>Show answers and reasoning</summary>

1. Self-attention mixes information across permitted positions; the MLP applies a position-wise transformation with shared weights.
2. The residual connection adds the sublayer output to its input: $x_{out}=x_{in}+F(x_{in})$. It preserves a direct path through the block while allowing the sublayer to contribute a learned transformation.

</details>
